title: Space: Beyond Our World
description: From our nearest star to the first footprints on another world—five steps into space.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us. And the Sun is so huge that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it!

questions.question: The Sun lights up our days. What lights up our nights, even though it makes no light of its own?
questions.hint: It looks like a different shape on different nights
questions.explanation: Moonlight is really sunlight bouncing off Moon dust. And the Moon drifts about 1.5 inches farther from Earth every year, as fast as your fingernails grow!

questions.question: People first walked on the Moon in what year?
questions.explanation: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 landed, and about 600 million people watched on TV. That was around one out of every five people on Earth back then!

questions.question: Who was the first person to step onto the Moon in 1969?
questions.hint: He was the commander of Apollo 11
questions.explanation: Buzz Aldrin followed him 19 minutes later. Armstrong said, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." He said he meant "a man." Listen closely!

questions.question: Neil Armstrong's bootprints are still on the Moon, more than 50 years later! Why haven't they been wiped away?
choices: Moon dust is sticky like glue
questions.hint: Think about what blows sand around at the beach
questions.explanation: With almost no air, the Moon has no wind or rain. Scientists think the prints could last millions of years, until tiny specks of space dust slowly sand them away.
